_about: SpriteCook prompts for the illustrated offerings. Common settings: generate_game_art, model gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, pixel false, mode assets, bg_mode transparent, aspect 1:1, width/height 384, style_asset_ids [061fc1f9-2d8c-4b66-9377-e18cf5ba3407] (the approved three-pistachios illustration). Each prompt is followed by the shared suffix below; rare finds also get the rare suffix.
_suffix: Rendered as a precious still-life object with soft moonlit glow and a few tiny sparkles around it. Single isolated object, three-quarter view, centred, transparent background, no hands, no text, no readable writing.
_rare_suffix: A rare treasure with a subtle luminous aura.
sea-glass-pillow: A perfect smooth piece of frosted green sea-glass with softly tumbled rounded edges.
tide-stone: A smooth luminous tide-stone with a shifting sea-glass green gleam glowing just beneath its surface.
lantern-shard: A translucent green sea-glass shard partly wrapped in a strip of soft charcoal-grey cloth.
daisy-pin: A tiny silver daisy brooch pin with delicate engraved petals.
warm-stone: A smooth grey river stone with a faint warm golden glow at its centre.
hair-ribbon: A soft rose-mauve silk ribbon tied in a loose loop around a small green sea-glass bead.
sweater-thread: A single fine silver-white thread tied in one tiny deliberate knot, its ends curling loosely.
brass-key: A small ornate antique brass key with a decorative bow.
rook-button: An old-fashioned silver button engraved with a tiny rook bird.
tiny-bell: A tiny old silver bell, beautifully tarnished, with a small loop at the top.
old-map: A torn fragment of an old parchment map showing one coastline and two small hand-drawn ink marks, edges browned with age.
tiny-compass: A miniature antique silver compass whose needle points north-west.
slate: A rain-dark, beautifully smooth piece of slate with one natural pale line running through it like lightning.
juniper: A fresh juniper sprig with dusty blue berries, tied neatly with black thread.
sea-worn-wood: A small piece of sea-worn dark driftwood smoothed into the shape of a crooked wing.
white-pebble: A small smooth white pebble with a single sea-glass green vein running through it.
black-feather: A glossy black rook feather with a faint green iridescent sheen.
feather-thread: A glossy black feather with dark silver thread wrapped around its quill, the loose thread looped through one small silver chain link.
open-clasp: A polished dark silver jewellery clasp left open, set with a small green sea-glass bead, on a short length of fine chain.
velvet-ribbon: A narrow strip of dark teal velvet ribbon folded once, soft side up, its pile catching the light.
mirror-chain: A short loose length of gunmetal chain coiled gracefully.
silver-anklet: A thin silver anklet chain with one green sea-glass bead, left unfastened in a loose circle.
rare-first-light: A sea-glass shard so pale it looks silver, with a deep green glow at its centre.
rare-moonbloom-seed: A closed pearl-pale moon-bloom seedpod, impossibly light and softly luminous.
rare-double-feather: Two glossy black feathers bound together at the stems with a translucent glowing green thread.
rare-pocket-watch: A stopped antique silver pocket watch lying open, its hands frozen at 3:17, the case engraved with a coastline.
rare-green-opal: A sea-green opaline cabochon gem, milky at the edges and deep green in its depths.
rare-locket: A tiny empty oval silver locket, open on its hinge.
rare-chain-crescent: A single crescent-shaped dark silver chain link set with a green glass bead.
rare-rook-token: A heavy blackened-silver token shaped like a small rook bird, worn smooth at the edges, with one tiny sea-glass dot for an eye.
morrow-silver-thread: A perfectly straight length of silver thread laid out with ceremonial neatness.
morrow-green-stone: One immaculate polished green pebble, flawless and unscratched.
morrow-button: An old mother-of-pearl button resting on a small, neatly folded scrap of linen.
ink-hair-tie: A simple dark hair tie looped around a tiny smooth stone.
ink-paper-star: A tiny folded origami star made of black paper.
ink-key: A very small antique iron key.
pip-ribbon: A teal satin ribbon in a loose, lively twist, as if just dropped from a beak.
pip-shiny-washer: An extremely shiny little metal washer gleaming proudly.
pip-leaf: A perfectly ridiculous curly leaf, spiralled and whimsical.
